## Quarto Spark Lines

In Quarto reports using R, you can create sparklines—small, compact charts that show trends without axes, legends, or unnecessary labels.

They are particularly useful for your Admissions, LMS, Rankings, and University Performance reports.

Since you generate reports in both HTML and Typst PDF, I recommend using ggplot2 for sparklines. It works with both formats.

| KPI | Value | Trend |
|---|---:|---|
| Applications | 25,480 | Small line chart |
| Enrolments | 8,250 | Small rising trend |
| Conversion Rate | 32.4% | Small fluctuating trend |


### What is a sparkline?
A sparkline is a miniature chart, usually displayed alongside a KPI.

A sparkline typically has:
- No X-axis or Y-axis labels.
- No gridlines or legend.
- Minimal margins.
- A thin line, sometimes with a highlighted final point.
- Consistent scaling when comparing similar metrics.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

sparkline <- function(data, x, y, color = "#174EA6") {

  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = {{ y }})) +
    geom_line(color = color, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(
      data = ~ dplyr::slice_max(
        .x, {{ x }}, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE
      ),
      color = color,
      size = 2
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1)
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 0.6
#| out-width: "45%"
library(tidyverse)

admissions <- tibble(  month = 1:12,  applications = c(    120, 180, 220, 350, 420, 580,
    720, 850, 920, 1100, 1250, 1480  )
)
p <- admissions %>%  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = applications)) +  geom_line(    color = "#174EA6",    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +  geom_point(    data = ~ slice_max(.x, month, n = 1),    color = "#174EA6",    size = 2
  ) +  theme_void() +  theme(    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)  )

p

sparkline(admissions, month, applications)


```
